new_statements.rule_in_words: Chaari is treated as a register-tone language with two tone levels (H, L), like all South Bauchi West lects other than Zaar and Guus; tone is lexical on every morpheme and is morphologically active (imperative sg H vs pl LHL replacing the verb's lexical tones; sg/pl pronoun oppositions carried by tone). No source says anything about word stress or accent -- neither a stress rule nor a statement that stress is absent.
new_statements.exceptions: None; Caron (2003/2006) cautions that his first Chaari survey was very short and 'not very reliable'; the 2014 chapter rests on a later couple-of-weeks lexical/morphological survey.
new_statements.domain_note: Tone statements concern lexical items and inflectional paradigms in citation/elicitation form; no word- vs phrase-level prosodic domain is discussed. The two-tone-levels remark is a group-level comparative statement in which Chaari is one of the explicitly sampled languages, not a dedicated phonological analysis of Chaari.
new_statements.identity_note: Glottolog dans1239 'Chaari' (historically labelled Danshe) = Cha'ari/Cààrí [cxh], created by ISO 639-3 CR 2022-030 from the old Zeem [zua] cluster. Caron's 'Cààrí (Danche)' data and the SIL 'Cha'ari' wordlist (collected in Danshe village, Toro LGA, Bauchi State) both refer to this variety. The sister lects Zeem [zem], Tulai [tvi], Dokshi/Lushi [dsk] and Dyarim [dyr, dyar1234] are distinct glottocodes; Dyarim (Blench 2005/2007, three phonetic tone levels, no stress statement) is already catalogued separately and its description must not be transferred to Chaari. The two-tone-levels statement quoted is a South-Bauchi-West group-level remark in which Chaari is one of the explicitly sampled languages.

sources.note: Nothing on stress. Introduction (PDF p.3): 'Zaar and Gùùs have three tone levels, the others only two' -- Cààrí (Chaari) is the Zeem-cluster language sampled among 'the others'; tone-marked Cààrí (Danche) TAM and pronoun paradigms (PDF pp.8, 15); author warns 'The survey of Cààrí was very short and the data collected is not very reliable.'

sources.note: Nothing on stress. Sect. 8.3 'Phonetic inventory' gives consonant and vowel charts from 222-item wordlists (Cha'ari list taken in Danshe village); Appendix F: 'The transcriptions are preliminary since there was no in-depth analysis of tones or other phonological or phonetic features.' Sect. 3: prior work on Cha'ari limited to Shimizu 1978 (seven words) and CAPRO 2004 (ethnographic).

First-hand Chaari data from a later lexical/morphological survey ('a couple of weeks'); sect. 4.2.2 (PDF p.14, printed p.13): 'In Chaari, the tone patterns of the Imperative are H for singular and LHL for plural' -- tone is lexical and morphologically active; all Chaari forms tone-marked.
